newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mostly firmer, new highs set.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mostly firmer, new highs set.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed mostly firmer after setting contract highs in the first four positions, boosted by rising product prices and bullish sentiment on charts, floor sources said.
They noted funds were active rolling long positions out of August into September and estimated that around 1,500 to 2,000 lots of fund longs had been rolled forward.

There was talk that cash cattle could trade $1 higher next week at $65 per cwt although there was some concern that the current futures premium to cash was too wide with the first delivery day for the August contract less than two week away.
"It is a fairly large premium but it could disappear in an instant. I don't think anyone is selling yet with delivery expectations," one floor trader said.

Outright buyers in August live cattle included E.D. and F. Man International and R.J. O'Brien while ADM Investor Services was a buyer of October. R.B. and H. Financial Services and ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp were sellers of August with Rand Financial Services a seller of October.
August live cattle closed up 0.225 cents a lb at 67.65 cents after setting a contract high of 67.85 cents. Cash trade this week has been mostly at $64 per cwt (64 cents a lb).
Other months finished up 0.675 cent to down 0.050 cent.
Feeder cattle futures closed mostly lower with the decline seen largely as a downside technical correction after recent strength.
The latest CME feeder cattle index, for July 24, was down $0.05 at $82.12.
Floor sources said Refco was a net buyer of August feeders while several firms, including Cargill Investor Services, were active buying October/selling August.
August feeders finished down 0.200 cent at 82.650 cents a lb. Other months were down 0.250 cent to up 0.100 cent.
